newsitem.title: USA: EquiMed revised 1996 earnings widen loss.
newsitem.headline: EquiMed revised 1996 earnings widen loss.

text.p: EquiMed Inc on Tuesday posted a revised 1996 loss of $31.1 million, or $1.14 per share, compared with a previously reported unaudited loss of $15.8 million, or $0.57.
Revenues for the year were $99.1 million, the company said, compared with its previous unaudited report of $99.7 million of revenues.

The revised net loss includes the effect of an extraordinary first-quarter charge relating to the early extinguishment of debt, a non-recurring item resulting from the change from S Corporation to C Corporation tax status, a loss associated with the sale of the ophthalmology division effective November 1, 1996 and additional tax accruals.
The total of these items was $39.2 million. Without them, 1996 net income would have been $7.9 million, or $0.29 a share.
EquiMed officials were not immediately available for further comment. Its initial 1996 results were released March 31.

EquiMed provides medical practice management services to its affiliated oncology centers and medical practices. It also provides data processing, billing, accounting, collections, and other administrative and outsourcing services to the health care industry.
